en: The Legend of the Elder Anuruddha The Chapter on the Buddhas, Number Six I was once a king named Mahinda, ruler of the earth. At that time, there appeared in the world the Buddha Kassapa. Having heard of the Teacher, I went to him with my retinue. Approaching the Great Sage, I paid homage at his feet. Then the Teacher, out of compassion for me, preached the Dhamma. Hearing the Dhamma, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. I offered a golden parasol to the Teacher, the One with Vision. And I made this aspiration: "May I be the chief attendant of this Buddha. By that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. In every birth, I have been a king, lord of the earth. For eighty-four thousand aeons, I have never known a lower realm. I have always been a wheel-turning monarch, a lord of the four quarters. Now, having passed away from that state, I am born here in the human world. I am the son of King Suddhodana, born into the Sakyan clan. I am the chief attendant of the Tathāgata, the One with Vision. I am the Elder Anuruddha, possessed of the divine eye. Through the power of that former aspiration, I have obtained these five supernormal powers. I dwell in the bliss of the first jhāna, free from sensual desire. I am one who has transcended the world, a sage who has reached the further shore. This is the legacy of the Elder Anuruddha.
“O Blessed One, I spoke to Sumedha,
the eldest in the world, the bull among men,
as he dwelt in seclusion.”
I saw the Leader of the World.
Having approached the Sambuddha,
Sumedha, the Leader of the World;
Raising my hands in añjali,
I made this request to the Supreme Buddha:
"Have compassion, O Great Hero."
O eldest of the world, bull among men:
I shall provide a lamp for you as you meditate at the foot of a tree.
That wise one,
the self-become, the best among speakers,
consented; having pierced through the trees, he emerged.
I then yoked the chariot;
I gave a thousand-fold offering to the Buddha,
the Kinsman of the World.
Having blazed for seven days,
my lamps were extinguished;
by that serene confidence of mind, [I attained peace].
And through my volition and aspiration,
having cast off the human body,
I was reborn in a celestial mansion.
Having been reborn in the divine state,
his celestial mansion was well-constructed;
it blazed forth on all sides.
This is the fruit of giving a lamp:
at that time, I shone for a hundred yojanas in every direction.
I surpass all the gods;
this is the fruit of giving lamps.
For thirty eons, I was the lord of the gods.
I exercised the sovereignty of the gods;
no one held me in contempt—
this is the fruit of giving a lamp.
And twenty-eight times I was a wheel-turning monarch;
day and night I behold—
At that time, throughout a league on all sides,
I beheld the thousandfold world-system with my wisdom within the Teacher’s dispensation.
Having attained the divine eye—
this is the fruit of the gift of a lamp.
The Perfectly Enlightened One named Sumedha,
Thirty thousand eons ago,
with a mind full of serene confidence, I gave that island to him.
The four analytical knowledges,
these eight liberations,
and the six direct knowledges have been realized.
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, indeed, the Elder Venerable Anuruddha spoke these verses.
This is the fourth legend (apadāna) of the Elder Anuruddha.
